the_complete_list_of_what_mode_1_writes: [edi+0x18] = an id looked up from the entity id array (mode 1 only)
[edi+0x24], [edi+0x2C], [edi+0x28] = three FLOATS, i.e. the entity ORIGIN
why_this_is_the_answer_to_the_original_q: the goal has been to give an entity an eType and an origin so the client draws it
mode 1 is precisely the operation that writes the origin as three floats
and the three floats are computed by 0x6715D0, 0x6714D0 and 0x671550 from the accumulated scratch values, so the position is derived from the mode 3 / mode 4 accumulators
that means a three-operation delta (mode 3, mode 4, mode 1) is exactly what places an entity at a chosen position
the_immediate_next_step: read 0x6715D0, 0x6714D0 and 0x671550 to learn how each float is derived from the scratch values
then choose mode 3 and mode 4 values that produce the desired x, y, z
mode 1 also needs its 2-bit inline value and, when the id width is non-zero, an id index - those are cheap to supply
